questions.question: Is LeetCode-style grinding actually going away as interview prep, or just changing?
questions.answer_summary: Multiple 2026 outlets debated whether 'LeetCode is dying'; the consensus in coverage is that it's evolving (companies still test DSA fundamentals but are adapting formats) rather than disappearing outright.
sources: https://news.google.com (Built In: 'LeetCode Is Dying, But What Will Come Next?', May 2026)

questions.question: What happened with the Columbia student who built an AI tool to cheat in technical interviews?
questions.answer_summary: Roy Lee built 'Interview Coder,' was suspended from/withdrew from Columbia over it, then raised funding (reported as $5.3M, later $15M from a16z) to build Cluely, a startup marketed around helping users 'cheat on everything.'

questions.question: Did other students respond to the Cluely/Interview Coder controversy?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — Columbia students launched 'Truely,' reported as 'the anti-Cluely,' an AI-detection tool built specifically to counter interview-cheating software.

questions.question: Is using AI during an actual interview considered cheating by companies?
questions.answer_summary: Coverage is split: some outlets frame it outright as cheating, while others (e.g., a 'Is Using AI in a Job Interview Cheating? It Depends' piece) argue the ethics hinge on transparency and stated company policy rather than the tool itself.
sources: https://news.google.com (Built In: 'Is Using AI in a Job Interview Cheating? It Depends,' Feb 2026)

questions.question: Are big tech companies banning or allowing AI use in interviews?
questions.answer_summary: Reports genuinely conflict: one 2026 piece says Google is 'embracing' candidate AI-assistant use, while a 2025 piece reports Google shifted toward more in-person interviews specifically because of a surge in AI-aided candidates; Adobe's leadership reportedly welcomes AI use while other employers remain hesitant.

questions.question: What do engineers say they now need beyond raw coding-test skill to get hired?
questions.answer_summary: Business Insider profiles of experienced engineers and a startup CTO report interviewers now weight system design, judgment, and collaboration/AI-era skills more heavily alongside DSA fundamentals.

questions.question: Are there dedicated AI mock-interview products built specifically to fill a practice gap LeetCode doesn't cover?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — Hacker News Show HN launches (e.g., Crackr, Neuraprep, CipherAI, LeetPro) explicitly cite 'LeetCode wasn't actually preparing me... for the pressure of a real technical interview' as their founding motivation.

questions.question: Is there a public real-world case of someone using AI to pass a top-tier technical interview?
questions.answer_summary: Gizmodo reported a case of a student using AI tools to pass Amazon's technical interview, receiving an offer, and then being reported by someone else.

questions.question: Has the interview-cheating debate reached frontier AI labs themselves?
questions.answer_summary: Built In published a piece specifically framing an 'Anthropic cheating scandal' in relation to whether it marks 'the end of the coding interview,' indicating the controversy extends beyond candidate-side tools.
sources: https://news.google.com (Built In: 'Is Anthropic's Cheating Scandal the End of the Coding Interview?', Feb 2026)

questions.question: How are AI-focused startups running technical hiring differently now?
questions.answer_summary: A Business Insider piece on hiring at 'the hottest AI coding startups' describes bootcamp-style vetting, work trials, and 'token burn' tests replacing some traditional interview formats.
